profile.headline: Software Engineer at Stedi
profile.summary: Persistent, determined, resourceful, creative, detail-oriented Senior Frontend Engineer with over 7 years of experience building complex React apps with Redux, Recoil, Typescript, Next.js, Python/Django, Vercel, and Github/Gitlab. Developed migration plan of complex features for architectural shift in app serving millions of monthly active users, planning for the future as much as maintaining the current feature set. Passionate about functional programming concepts and using full-stack knowledge to determine the most efficient solutions to complex problems.

positions.title: Senior Frontend Engineer
positions.description:
Collaborated with product managers, engineering teams and partnerships to determine a transition plan for a set of features in the Zap editor while we rebuild the data structure on which a Zap is built. Ensured continuity of user features while planning for architectural code resilience, and system efficiency and flexibility to support future features.

Designed A/B/C testing framework using Split.io and Typescript to support conditional UI experiments based on developer-defined parameters. Prioritized developer experience and flexibility of test conditions, allowing us to change parameters or priority of a test without making code changes. Extended existing Split.io framework with these features to support user testing needs.

positions.title: Frontend Engineer
positions.description:
Built complex UIs from sigma mockups using React, Redux and Typescript deployed to millions of users every month. Thrived in a rapidly changing company, from monorepo to microservices, and from 50 employees to over 500 today.

Designed semantic HTML to ensure accessibility of interfaces and good document structure. Weighed the pros and cons of using libraries with "built-in accessibility" over custom components.

Conducted interviews for frontend engineer positions on behalf of the company and mentored junior colleagues to strengthen the team

positions.title: Web Developer | Lead Preservation Artist
positions.description:
At Cinemalab, I recognized that our website lacked organization, had poor readability and navigability, and lacked valuable information. I taught myself HTML and CSS to overhaul the website, dramatically improving readability, aesthetics and content. I used Illustrator and Photoshop to design the new logo. The website is now a modern platform for the company to reach new clients and is a great representation of the company's work. I used the website re-design as a launchpad into new marketing ventures, and brainstormed and implemented creative new ways to expand the client base.

One theme applies to all my work at Cinemalab: I love having a problem to solve and the freedom to solve it. I developed innovative and unprecedented strategies to successfully restore severely decayed film, further securing the reputation of Cinemalab as one of the premiere preservation-focused photochemical labs in the country.

Encompassing all of this is my dedication to excellence in content. The talented clients of Cinemalab helped me to develop a good eye for quality, and to constantly push myself to grow, to learn new skills and to expand my expertise. This resulted in my coordination of the preservation of over 40,000 feet of film from clients such as UCLA, the Film Noir Foundation and George Eastman House. I physically 
inspected and repaired each reel of film for printing and scanning, which required a great deal of 
patience and attention to detail.  

Film Repair and Cleaning
Vinegar Syndrome
Nitrate Degradation
Projection
Optical Printing
Color Correction
Color Mastering
Customer Service
Web Design

positions.title: Intern: editor, graphic design, marketing
positions.description:
The summer of 2012 was an exciting time to be interning with Serac Adventure Films. They had just 
released their award-winning film, “High Ground” and were working on another called “Out Living It”. I created trailers, posters and bonus DVD content for both films to generate excitement, and I captured b-roll footage for use in “Out Living It”. I also played a vital role in the success of the Outside Adventure Film School from Outside Magazine. We taught students the basics of filmmaking while at the 2012 
X Games in Aspen, such as how to use the cameras and strategies for capturing great shots. Later, we showed them how to edit their films with Final Cut Pro X. During the course, I got to know the students and documented their experiences, and upon their graduation, I gave them personalized diplomas, edited in Photoshop to look like Outside Magazine covers. My expertise in Photoshop, video production and editing was instrumental in the success of the school, and inspired and empowered the students to create their own video content.

projects.description: Used Weebly to install a website for a busy real estate agent that is both easy to manage and powerful. Designed a new logo and installed additional features such as an MLS search engine.

projects.title: Don't Bet On Women
projects.description: "Don't Bet On Women", known under the alternate title "All Women Are Bad" (both intriguing...) comes to us from the Museum of Modern Art in New York City. A delightfully sexist comedic romp, the film was though to be largely lost until the 1970s. We're working with a dupe neg made in the 70s, and unfortunately it is rather scratched and dirty. The reels also came to us out of order on huge 2,000 footers, so we had to cut them apart and re-sync the sound based on visual cues. However, a lot can be done with timing and gamma correction, and we've ended up with a beautiful final product that will keep this movie around for the next 1,000 years!
